item.title: Mortgage Rates Hit 6.71%, Their Highest Level Since July 2025
item.description: Higher costs for home loans have put a squeeze on the housing market, adding pressure to consumers already struggling with elevated inflation.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth A. Harris

item.title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July
item.description: The trade deficit bounced back up last month as spending on data centers to feed the A.I. boom drove up imports.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson

item.title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
item.description: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump (Book)
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is facing a complicated challenge as he tries to cool global energy prices while increasing economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Dutch Central Bank Cuts Gold Reserves in U.S., Citing ‘Geopolitical Unrest’
item.description: The Netherlands moved some 90 tons of gold out of the Federal Reserve Bank in New York, the second European nation this year to announce it had decreased or eliminated U.S. gold holdings.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Federal Reserve Bank of New York
item.media:description: Olaf Sleijpen, president of the central bank of the Netherlands, in Amsterdam in March. “We have improved the tradeability of our gold reserves,” he said.

item.title: Schools Aiding Minority Students Could Lose Tax-Exempt Status
item.description: Also, Gloria Steinem died at 92. Here’s the latest at the end of Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cullen
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times

item.title: Volkswagen Plans to Cut 50,000 Jobs
item.description: Facing growing competition from China and rapidly advancing technology, the German auto giant said its board had approved a “comprehensive” overhaul.
item.dc:creator: James Paton
item.media:credit: Felix Schmitt for The New York Times
item.media:description: Facing intense pressure and Chinese competition, Volkswagen has slashed its annual production targets and plans to cut its model lineup.

item.title: Trump to Break Ground on Arch Before Getting Approval
item.description: Doug Burgum, the interior secretary, announced plans to start work on the site of the 250-foot-tall triumphal arch. Final approval of the project is still pending.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:description: President Trump has said that the 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery must be taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

item.title: Federal Prosecutors Charge ICE Agent With Lying About Minnesota Shooting
item.description: The charges are a rare instance of President Trump’s Justice Department accusing a federal agent of breaking the law while on the job.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith and Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: Federal agents near the scene of the shooting in Minneapolis in January.

item.title: Proposal for White House Visitor Screening Center Advances
item.description: A federal panel again paved the way for one of President Trump’s construction projects, even as it heard opposition to another proposal to fence in a park north of the White House.
item.dc:creator: Aishvarya Kavi
item.media:credit: Jared Soares for The New York Times
item.media:description: The entrance to the proposed screening center would be in Sherman Park, southeast of the White House.

item.title: Clancy’s Lawyer, Kevin Reddington, Became a Hero to Her Supporters
item.description: The themes present in Lindsay Clancy’s trial are not unfamiliar to Mr. Reddington, a veteran defense lawyer.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:description: Kevin Reddington, Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer, speaking to reporters outside Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass.

item.title: Gloria Steinem, Personification of the Feminist Movement, Dies at 92
item.description: She challenged sexist assumptions, helping women develop a sense of self-worth and gain a measure of equality at work, at home and in society at large.
item.dc:creator: Katharine Q. Seelye
item.media:description: Ms. Steinem at a rally in 1968. “The truth will set you free,” she liked to say, “but first it will piss you off.”

item.title: Steinem’s Home, Where Feminism Flourished, Will Remain a Gathering Place
item.description: Following Ms. Steinem’s death on Wednesday, her foundation said her Upper East Side home would become a permanent space for organizing and activism.
item.dc:creator: Anna Kodé
item.media:description: Gloria Steinem, left, sits with Ms. magazine co-founder Patricia Carbine in 1987.

item.title: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and Others Pay Tribute to Gloria Steinem
item.description: After Ms. Steinem’s death at 92, celebrities and politicians reflected on her decades of activism for women’s rights and equality.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:description: Gloria Steinem “pushed open doors not just for herself, but for literally millions of women behind her,” Hillary Clinton, the former secretary of state and presidential candidate, said in a tribute on Thursday.

item.title: In a First, a Pig Kidney Kept a Patient Alive Until He Got a Human One
item.description: Tim Andrews was the first patient to receive a genetically modified pig kidney as a “bridge” to a human organ transplant.
item.dc:creator: Roni Caryn Rabin
item.media:credit: Cheryle St. Onge for The New York Times
item.media:description: Tim Andrews lived with a kidney from a genetically modified pig for nine months. The pig kidney gave him a reprieve from dialysis treatments.

item.title: Missouri Supreme Court Delivers Win for Democrats in Redistricting Case
item.description: The court said a map redrawn to benefit Republicans could not be used in November and said voters should decide on the new boundaries. The state attorney general vowed to appeal the decision.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith
item.media:description: The Missouri State Capitol in Jefferson City.

item.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Limits
item.description: The justices have been asked to weigh in again on the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict mail voting — this time on whether the plans violate the Constitution.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: Administration lawyers asked the Supreme Court to clear the way for a new rule that prohibits the Postal Service from delivering ballots to voters in states that do not share voter data with the federal agency.

item.title: Judge Suggests Trump Mail-In Voting Rules Could Cause ‘Major Disenfranchisement’
item.description: Judge Indira Talwani said the Postal Service appeared to be trying a haphazard “experiment” with a new rule that could result in valid ballots being tossed.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:description: An official picking up a mail-in ballot drop box at the Lackawanna County Government Center in Scranton, Pa., in 2024.

item.title: The Start-Up That Helps People Die
item.description: Medical aid in dying is now legal in New York. A team of clinical professionals decided to create a practice to help their clients die on their own terms.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg and Erin Schaff

item.title: Maria Bartiromo Is Out at Fox News
item.description: The host, who appeared on Fox Business and Fox News, had been with the network for more than 12 years.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple
item.media:description: Fox did not give a reason for Maria Bartiromo’s abrupt departure. She has been an ardent supporter of President Trump.

item.title: What Did Jurassic Forests Sound Like? Like This.
item.description: Scientists spent over a decade reconstructing the calls of nine species of ancient insects to create the first accurate Jurassic soundscape.
item.dc:creator: Annie Roth
item.category: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
item.media:description: By studying the fossilized wings of ancient insects as well as the bioacoustics of their living relatives, researchers were able to use computer modeling and machine learning to replicate their sounds.

item.title: Tesla Begins Offering Rides in a Car Without a Steering Wheel
item.description: The new Cybercab embodies Elon Musk’s vision of cars that drive themselves, but it is not clear when the vehicle will be widely available.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:description: The Cybercab embodies the longtime ambition of Elon Musk, Tesla’s chief executive, to create cars that could steer, brake and navigate autonomously.

item.title: MAGA Is Feeding a Separatist Surge in Canada
item.description: Drawing inspiration from MAGA, separatists in Alberta are pushing for a break away from Canada.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Gillespie and Chelsee Ivan

item.title: Why a Doctor Told Gloria Steinem: ‘You Must Promise Me Two Things’
item.description: Gloria Steinem got to be who she was because of a pre-Roe abortion.
item.dc:creator: Jill Filipovic

item.title: Travis Kelce’s New Ohio Home Has Neighbors Buzzing With Excitement About Taylor Swift
item.description: The wealthy enclave of Bratenahl, Ohio, has been aflutter after learning that Travis Kelce purchased a Lake Erie mansion.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Contrera
item.media:description: Bratenahl is a wealthy suburb on Lake Erie near Cleveland.
